mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that boosts equity markets, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate above 6% triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as high unemployment indicates a slowing economy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between GDP growth and housing market activity drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a strong economy and housing market boost consumer spending and confidence.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals a decrease in supply chain activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between federal funds rate and inflation rate drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as a high inflation rate and low federal funds rate indicate an overheating economy.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales signals a strong consumer spending trend, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between unemployment rate and payroll employment drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a low unemployment rate and high payroll employment indicate a strong labor market.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 1% triggers a positive signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as an extremely low federal funds rate indicates a highly accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).
